class.name: FileSystemDatabase
class.brief_description: A [NetwDatabaseBackend] that stores each record as one [DictionaryRecord] file.
class.description: A record lives at [code]<root>/<table>/<id>.<ext>[/code]. The root folds [member app_id] and the open slot into [member base_dir], so two saves of one game never meet. [codeblock lang=text] base_dir └── app_id └── slot └── table └── id.res [/codeblock] Every read and write goes straight to disk through [ResourceLoader] and [ResourceSaver]. There is no cache, so [member NetwDatabase.warm_policy] is ignored and a write is durable the moment it returns. [codeblock] var db := NetwDatabase.new() var fs := FileSystemDatabase.new() fs.base_dir = "user://saves" fs.use_text_format = true # readable .tres instead of binary .res db.backend = fs [/codeblock] A subdirectory under the slot root that no registered table claims is a ghost table. Initialization reports each one as a warning and never deletes data on its own, because a directory the schema stopped naming is more often a migration than garbage. Two live backends pointing at one slot root is rejected with an error rather than tolerated: both would write the same files and each would report the other's tables as ghosts. Share one [NetwDatabase] instead, or give them different [member base_dir].

members.member: Application scope folded into the storage path ahead of the save slot. Leave it empty to store slots directly under [member base_dir]. Set it to keep several games sharing one [member base_dir] from colliding.

Root directory for every table subdirectory. Point it at [code]user://saves[/code] for a shipped game: a [code]res://[/code] root is rewritten to [code]user://[/code] outside the editor, because an exported project's resources are read-only.

Picks the record file extension. [code]true[/code] writes the readable [code].tres[/code] text form, and [code]false[/code] the compact binary [code].res[/code]. [ResourceSaver] dispatches on the extension and rejects one it does not recognize, so these are the engine's own two and not a format this class invents.
